read.thesis: Mosaic cut 2026 capex to $1.2B and targets under $1B in 2027 while idling phosphate on sulfur costs; Q4 flagged as EBITDA trough, with phosphate supply still constrained by sulfur.

utilisation.quote: Florida footprint generally is in the low- to mid-60%

capex.peers_comment: Some producers in Asia have begun exploring nontraditional sources of sulfur including reclamation from gyp stacks and the restart of long dormant sulfur mines.

triggers.label: 2026 capex cut $1.5B → $1.2B
triggers.quote: The 2026 spend was cut to $1.2 billion from $1.5 billion

triggers.label: Phosphate idled on sulfur costs
triggers.quote: we are focused on meeting our customers' needs as best we can while optimizing netbacks and managing inventory

triggers.label: North America fall demand stronger
triggers.quote: the fall demand for phosphate in North America has been, coming much stronger than, many of us anticipated
triggers.highlight: much stronger than, many of us anticipated

triggers.label: Q4 DAP guided $820–840/t
triggers.quote: DAP Price Guidance -- $820 to $840 per tonne for the fourth quarter

triggers.label: Q3 phosphate volume 1.6 → 1.4Mt
triggers.quote: production curtailments implemented to align with affordable sulfur availability

guidance.quote: The 2026 spend was cut to $1.2 billion from $1.5 billion
we expect 2027 SG&A to be below $500 million
we expect realized prices in cost of goods sold to be in the range of $800 to $850 per ton
For ammonia, we expect cost to be in the range of $590 to $610 per ton
this will result in realized stripping margins in the mid-$300s per ton
Potash Sales Volume Guidance -- 2.3 million to 2.6 million tonnes for the fourth quarter
we remain on track to generate nearly $135 million in 2026
we expect to generate positive free cash flow in the second half of this year

red_flags.label: Q4 EBITDA trough flagged
red_flags.quote: Q4 is gonna be a trough in terms of EBITDA especially in the phosphate segment

red_flags.label: Customer credit constrained
red_flags.quote: Customer credit remains constrained and we continue to be selective in extending credit.
